subject: Post-demo: Bench readout and next steps for pilot
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@sentra.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Bench readout and next steps for pilot

Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and clear next steps so we're all aligned: 

1) What we demoed
- Hosted inference readout against your internal prompt set (50k tokens total)
- Config: 2x A100 equiv, INT8 pipeline, KV caching enabled
- Visible outputs attached in redwood_bench_raw.csv and a short summary (redwood_bench_summary.pdf)

2) Key measured numbers (from our run)
- Median (p50) generation latency: ~36 ms/token
- Tail (p95) latency: ~210 ms/token (this includes initial KV-warm-up on cold start)
- Sustained throughput for concurrent 8 sessions: ~160 requests/sec under 128-token average responses
- Notes: we saw a 20–30% improvement after the KV warming phase (first 30s) and with request coalescing enabled.

3) Outstanding technical Qs you raised
- Impact of long contexts on p95 and memory growth
- How pipelined batching interacts with your 75ms SLO for interactive edges
- What an initial dedicated pool would look like (capacity + cost)

4) Proposed immediate next steps (pick one)
A) Pilot: 2-week dedicated pilot (reserved pool) with your typical traffic pattern + watch window — we provide bench scripts + priority support.
B) Proof artifact: we can run the same job in your account/region (we'll need access details) and produce a latency report tuned to your production prompts.

Please confirm which option you prefer and your timeline/priority (this month vs next quarter). If useful, I've attached the raw CSV and a one-pager. If there are internal stakeholders we should loop in (infra, SRE), let me know and I'll add them.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Hi Aditya — thanks for this and the run details. A few quick technical clarifications from our engineering side: 

- p95 calls: can you confirm whether that 210 ms is measured per-token or per-response? We run variable-length outputs (avg ~120 tokens).
- Concurrency profile: the 160 req/s number — was that steady-state after warm-up and with KV caching already populated?
- Memory usage: curious about peak GPU memory during the 128-token tests; our GPUs sit at ~95% capacity in some spikes.

I've attached a small trace set from our staging service (sentra_app_traces.zip) that shows our typical request arrival pattern. If you can annotate where the KV warm-up is showing up versus true tail behavior, that'd help our SREs.

Also, on the timeline: we have a leadership review on 6/25 — if we can get a tightened estimate by 6/22 that'd be ideal.

Appreciate it,
Alex
Alex Morgan | Staff Engineer, Sentra AI
alex@sentra.ai

Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Bench readout and next steps for pilot

Hi Alex — digging into the traces you sent. Short answers up front, then a little more detail below.

Short answers:
- The 210 ms number in our summary is p95 per-response for the benchmark run where average response length was ~128 tokens. We reported per-response not per-token in the PDF; the per-token breakdown is in the CSV.
- The 160 req/s was steady-state after a 30s warm-up with KV caching populated by a short prefix-loading pass. Without warm-up (cold start) p95 can be 2–3x higher for the first 30–60s.
- Peak GPU memory in that test was ~82% on a 80GB-class instance (model trimmed to INT8). Your observed 95% spikes sound like they could be coming from additional background jobs or larger context windows; if you can share an example request we can run it as a focused repro.

What we recommend for your SRE review on 6/25:
- Option 1 (recommended): run the bench job in your environment with our bench script (we'll provide the container). That will surface real shapes and give you the tightened estimates you need.
- Option 2: pilot with small dedicated pool (2-4 GPU equiv) for two weeks; we run against production-like traffic and hand off a final report.

Attached is a short primer on latency dynamics (redwood-latency-primer.pdf) that explains KV warm-up, coalescing, and typical tail behaviors for interactive workloads. If you want, we can jump on a 30-min runbook call for SRE on Mon/Tue next week.

Let me know which option you want to pursue and I'll coordinate the bench execution or schedule the call.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Staff Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com | +1 (617) 555-0147

Attachment(s): redwood-latency-primer.pdf (PDF)
